title: RIKEN confirms unauthorized access and malicious programs on Fugaku supercomputer operational servers
organization: RIKEN Center for Computational Science / Fugaku and RIKYU
summary: RIKEN's November 17 disclosure says an external intruder accessed Fugaku's internal operational network between November 10 and 13 through a public operational-status dashboard, altered multiple servers and installed malicious programs. Fugaku operations were suspended November 14. Names, email addresses, user IDs and stored external-service credentials associated with up to approximately 4,597 users may have been exposed; RIKEN says there is no concrete evidence research files were exfiltrated. The intruder attempted to access other systems using some obtained credentials. Exact exploit and actor remain unknown; affected users were told to revoke stored keys and rotate credentials.
sourceName: RIKEN official incident disclosure, published November 17, 2026
confidence: High for unauthorized access, server tampering and malicious programs; uncertain data exfiltration and secondary impact
connection: No verified shared malicious indicators, actor, exploited vulnerability or causal relationship with the November US service outages or Optimizely.

title: Osaki Electric ransomware halts smart-meter production and shipments
summary: Osaki Electric confirmed on November 18 that ransomware encrypted server data, detected around 10:35 a.m. Japan time on November 17. The company disconnected external network links and stopped production-related systems at its Saitama facility and affiliates Iwate Osaki Electric and Osaki Platech, suspending production and shipments of smart meters and other products. Restart date is unknown. Possible data exfiltration is under investigation, not confirmed. No evidence of electricity supply interruption or effects on U.S. utilities has been reported.

title: Oracle issues urgent Java security patches including CVE-2026-114938
summary: On November 17, Oracle released Java security updates addressing 11 Java SE vulnerabilities potentially remotely exploitable without authentication. CISA separately issued an urgent patching alert for CVE-2026-114938 ('Java4Shell'), describing a critical memory-corruption flaw in the x86-64 HotSpot JVM Base64 decoder that could permit unauthenticated remote code execution when reachable through vulnerable applications. Organizations should inventory Java runtimes, including bundled software and containers, and apply vendor fixes. The existence of the vulnerability and urgent patch guidance does not establish exploitation in the wild or a link to recent U.S. service outages.
sourceName: Oracle — November 2026 Critical Security Patch Update
confidence: High (vendor advisory); no confirmed exploitation in this reporting
connection: Java is used across banking, aviation, government and cloud infrastructure, but common use does not establish a technical connection to the November Microsoft 365, FAA, Chase, United Airlines, NSA Net or Optimizely incidents.

title: Optimizely scripts compromised across 178 organizations
summary: On November 16, attackers exploited Optimizely Web Experimentation to inject malicious JavaScript into customer sites associated with at least 178 organizations. Researchers identified cryptocurrency-address substitution, payment-card skimming, and conditional delivery of iOS exploit stages; successful iPhone compromise and the number of stolen cards are not established. On November 17 researchers also reported related malicious script delivery through Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and Minute.ly, with shared loader/infrastructure observations. Optimizely said it fixed the vulnerability and removed injected code. StorifyMe separately confirmed unauthorized JavaScript reached some customer integrations, said it removed code and disabled custom JavaScript, and reported no verified device compromise or data theft; investigation continues.
confidence: High (compromise)
connection: Confirmed shared compromised Optimizely scripts explain exposure across its customer websites. Researchers observed related malicious script infrastructure on Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and Minute.ly; this is evidence of a wider web-injection campaign, not proof all four services shared an entry-point or operator. No demonstrated link to FAA, Microsoft 365, Chase, United Airlines or NSA Net outages.

title: CISA confirms exploitation of Puppet Enterprise remote code execution flaw CVE-2026-115731
summary: CISA added CVE-2026-115731 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 17, 2026. Unsafe deserialization in Puppet Server report processing can allow a client with a CA-signed agent certificate to execute code as the Puppet Server service user. Weak certificate autosigning can make exploitation possible by unauthenticated remote attackers. Affected Puppet Enterprise branches have fixes in 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 and 2026.0.1. Federal remediation deadline: December 1, 2026. CISA confirms exploitation in the wild, but no specific victim, campaign, or actor has been publicly established in cited sources; this advisory is not a confirmed named-victim intrusion.
sourceName: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (added Nov. 17, 2026)
confidence: High (CISA known exploitation and vendor vulnerability); victim attribution unknown
connection: No verified shared actor, indicator, or technical causal connection with November 2026 Microsoft 365, FAA, banking, United Airlines, NSA Net, or Optimizely incidents.
